bull.b: The long-term PPA secures a critical power input for Phase 1 and reduces a major development uncertainty. Firm contracted capacity can improve the project's ability to attract a hyperscale tenant, support lease negotiations, and underpin a multi-year revenue platform.

Full Phase 1 permitting and active site work indicate that the project has moved beyond an early concept toward execution. The modular approach and targeted lower construction cost could improve capital efficiency, commissioning visibility, and potential project economics.

The PIPE and debt repayment materially improve near-term financial flexibility and preserve cash for development and leasing activities. A stronger capital base gives New Era more capacity to advance infrastructure milestones while pursuing additional project financing.

bear.b: Declining TTM revenue, widening losses, and sustained negative operating and free cash flow show that the existing business is not self-funding. Continued cash burn can increase reliance on external financing and make execution more sensitive to project delays.

The PPA and permitting progress do not yet represent a completed commercial project because the definitive Phase 1 lease remains unsigned. Delays or changes in scope, payment timing, or responsibilities could postpone construction, financing, and future revenue realization.

Phase 2 expansion depends on regulatory approval and a finalized funding structure, while substantial restricted cash limits immediate liquidity flexibility. These conditions could delay the planned 550 MW addition or require further capital before the broader campus is operational.
